answer: The marble-mirror wind test binds one identity to one polished stone: the claimant sets a marble slab on a named ridge, polishes one face to mirror the sky, and records how a morning zephyr bends a ribbon of smoke across the glass. Two ridge keepers compare the reflection, check the stone against the marble register, and confirm the reading within three days. A swapped slab, a painted mirror, or smoke blown by hand voids the season, burns an 80-credit stake, and bars the sponsor for two years. One honest test costs 80 credits; 1,000 fakes need 1,000 marble slabs polished and read by hand.
